book.foodindustrial.manual.category.t0.d: No machines: hand tools, passive devices placed in the world, vanilla campfires and furnaces, and what the world does by itself.

book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.history: Cod Liver Oil
In the 18th and 19th centuries, Nordic coasts rendered oil from cod livers.$(br)In the game it is boiled in a pot.
Hartshorn
In the 17th and 18th centuries, Europeans dry-distilled deer antlers into an ammonium carbonate leavening called hartshorn.$(br)In the game, the clay kiln dry-distils it.
Indigo
Ancient China fermented indigo plants into indigo dye; the saying that blue comes from the indigo plant is about it.$(br)In the game it ferments in a crock.
Kanten
In Edo-period Japan, people around Kyoto froze and thawed gelidium jelly outdoors through the winter to dry it into kanten (agar).$(br)In the game the drying rack does it in cold biomes.
Kelp Ash Soda

From the 17th to the 19th century, coastal people in Scotland, Normandy and elsewhere burned seaweed and leached soda and iodine from the ash.$(br)In the game, ash is burned on a campfire and leached in a leaching barrel.
Papaya Tenderising
In Central America, meat was wrapped in papaya leaves and latex to tenderise it.$(br)In the game, papaya latex is cut with a knife.
Potash and Pearl Ash
From antiquity to the 19th century, people leached wood ash with water and boiled the lye dry for potash.$(br)In the game it takes three steps: ash on a campfire, a leaching barrel and a pot.
Red Yeast Rice
Traditional Chinese koji rooms grew red yeast rice, widely used for wine and colouring by the Song dynasty.$(br)In the game the koji tray and the koji room make it, with random purity.
Boiling Saltpetre
In ancient China, nitre soil scraped from the foot of walls was leached, mixed with ash lye and boiled until saltpetre crystallised.$(br)The nitre soil, leaching barrel and pot of the game follow it.
Sea Salt and Bittern
Salt fields on the Chinese coast let seawater dry in shallow pans; the bittern left over set tofu.$(br)The salt pan in the game follows them.
Stevia
The Guarani of Paraguay sweetened mate with stevia leaves.$(br)In the game, stevia leaves are boiled in a pot for a sweet liquor.
Sulfur Fumigation
Dried fruit, candied fruit and white fungus were traditionally fumigated with burning sulfur in a closed room against browning and mould.$(br)The game uses the fumigation box.
Tapping Latex and Resin
The Olmecs of Central America already used rubber tree latex, and tapping pine resin is just as old.$(br)In the game, a knife cuts both.
Tartar
The Romans knew the tartar on the walls of wine casks; in 1769 Scheele made tartaric acid from it.$(br)In the game, wine kept cold in a wooden tank deposits tartar.

book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.koji_ro: Multiblock: the controller sits in the middle of the front face of a 3 × 3 × 3 shell. Any shell block may be an item, fluid or energy port for automation.

The Koji Room is a machine of the $(#5e9e3a)Workshop$() stage. Solid fermentation; fuel and water set the climate.$(br2)Recipe types: Solid Fermentation.$(br)Power: none.$(br)Modes: Koji trays, Shallow trays, switched in the screen.
book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.koji_tr: The Koji Tray is a device of the $(#a67c52)By Hand$() stage. Spreads four batches of grain to sprout or grow koji.$(br2)Recipe types: Solid Fermentation, Culture Work. Products made by hand have a purity cap; later stages make them purer.
book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.leach_b: The Leaching Barrel is a device of the $(#a67c52)By Hand$() stage. Water poured over ash or nitre soil; the liquor drains below.$(br2)Recipe types: Extraction, Adsorption and Membranes. Products made by hand have a purity cap; later stages make them purer.
book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.membran: The Membrane Separator is a machine of the $(#a35fc4)Biology and Fine Chemicals$() stage. Ultrafiltration, nanofiltration, RO and electrodialysis.$(br2)Recipe types: Adsorption and Membranes.$(br)Power: FE through any face that is not closed.$(br)Modes: Ultrafiltration, Nanofiltration, Reverse osmosis, Bipolar membrane electrodialysis, switched in the screen.
book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.mixer.t: The Mixer is a machine of the $(#3f7fc4)Industry$() stage. Blending; evens out purity; converts other mods' items.$(br2)Recipe types: Blending.$(br)Power: FE through any face that is not closed.$(br)Modes: Blending, Homogenizing, Normalizing, switched in the screen.$(br)Modules: High-Shear Emulsifying Head, Internal Mixer Rotors.
The Mortar is a device of the $(#a67c52)By Hand$() stage. Held, right-click an ingredient (or the reverse) to grind.$(br2)Recipe types: Grinding. Products made by hand have a purity cap; later stages make them purer.

book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.pot_sti: The Pot Still is a machine of the $(#5e9e3a)Workshop$() stage. Distilling and subliming; needs a condenser on top.$(br2)Recipe types: Distillation.$(br)Power: fuel (coal, charcoal or firewood).$(br)Modes: Distillation, Steam distillation, Sublimation, switched in the screen.$(br)Modules: Essential Oil Separator.

book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.salt_pa: The Salt Pan is a device of the $(#a67c52)By Hand$() stage. Sun-dries seawater into salt; neighbouring pans join.$(br2)Recipe types: Crystallization. Products made by hand have a purity cap; later stages make them purer.
book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.screw_p: The Screw Press is a machine of the $(#5e9e3a)Workshop$() stage. Hand-cranked pressing: juice, oil, gel dewatering.$(br2)Recipe types: Pressing.$(br)Power: a hand crank on top, turned with an empty hand.

book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.sieve.t: The Sieve is a device of the $(#a67c52)By Hand$() stage. Held, right-click an ingredient or bucket (or the reverse).$(br2)Recipe types: Solid-Liquid Separation. Products made by hand have a purity cap; later stages make them purer.
book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.solid_l: The Solid-Liquid Separator is a machine of the $(#3f7fc4)Industry$() stage. Pressing and separating; modules add filters and spinning.$(br2)Recipe types: Pressing, Solid-Liquid Separation.$(br)Power: FE through any face that is not closed.$(br)Modules: Filter Plates, Centrifuge Drum.
book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.spray_d: Multiblock: the controller sits in the middle of the front face of a 3 × 4 × 3 shell. Any shell block may be an item, fluid or energy port for automation.
The Spray Drying Tower is a machine of the $(#d0703a)Chemistry$() stage. Flash spray drying for heat-sensitive goods.$(br2)Recipe types: Drying.$(br)Power: FE through any face that is not closed.
book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.steepin: The Steeping Vat is a machine of the $(#5e9e3a)Workshop$() stage. Soaking, leaching, filtering, extracting; takes gases.$(br2)Recipe types: Solid-Liquid Separation, Extraction, Gas Absorption.$(br)Power: none.
book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.sterile: Multiblock: the controller sits in the middle of the front face of a 3 × 3 × 3 shell. Any shell block may be an item, fluid or energy port for automation. The middle layer repeats 1–4 times; taller runs more in parallel.

The Aseptic Fermenter is a machine of the $(#a35fc4)Biology and Fine Chemicals$() stage. Aseptic fermentation; a taller vessel makes more.$(br2)Recipe types: Liquid Fermentation.$(br)Power: FE through any face that is not closed.$(br)Modes: Aerated fermentation, Sealed, switched in the screen.
book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.stirred: The Stirred Reactor is a machine of the $(#3f7fc4)Industry$() stage. Liquid reactions; heats, cools, takes nitrogen and air.$(br2)Recipe types: Liquid-Phase Reaction.$(br)Power: FE through any face that is not closed.$(br)Modes: Reaction, Polymerization, switched in the screen.$(br)Modules: Corrosion-Resistant Lining, Vacuum Pump, Cryogenic Jacket, UV Lamp.
book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.stone_m: The Stone Mill is a machine of the $(#5e9e3a)Workshop$() stage. Hand-cranked grinding, dry or wet with water.$(br2)Recipe types: Grinding.$(br)Power: a hand crank on top, turned with an empty hand.$(br)Modes: Dry grinding, Wet grinding, switched in the screen.
book.foodindustrial.manual.entry.vanilla: Campfires, furnaces, smokers and blast furnaces also run the mod's drying, smoking and kiln recipes, one item in and one item out. Vanilla recipes come first.$(br2)The campfire is slowest, the smoker and blast furnace fastest; the blast furnace counts as the $(#5e9e3a)Workshop$() stage.
book.foodindustrial.manual.landing: This handbook walks through the tools, machines and processes of food industry, stage by stage.$(br2)Each chapter is one stage: $(#a67c52)By Hand$() works by hand and with the world, $(#5e9e3a)Workshop$() burns fuel or turns by hand, $(#3f7fc4)Industry$() runs on power, $(#d0703a)Chemistry$() does chemistry and $(#a35fc4)Biology and Fine Chemicals$() does fermentation and fine chemicals. Press R or U on any machine in JEI to see its recipes.
